report:
OA promjene koljenskog zgloba, izraženije u medijalnom kompartmentu FT zgloba.
Koštani edem medijalnog kondila femura te manjim dijelom medijalnog platoa tibije.
Brojne koštane apozicije zglobnih tijela.
Potpuni gubitak hrskavice u medijalnom dijelu zgloba uz stanjenu hrskavicu u lateralnom dijelu.
Veći izljev u zglobu. Baker cista veličine 6,3 cm. Ganglion cista 19 mm posterolateralnog dijela zglobne
čahure uz lat. epikondil femura.
Potpuna ruptura prednjeg križnog ligamenta.
Stražnji križni ligament urednog signala te se prati u kontinuitetu.
Kompleksna ruptura trupa i stražnjeg roga medijalnog meniska s ekstruzijom meniska van koštanog
okvira zgloba. Opisano prvenstveno na bazi deg. promjena.
Miksoidna degeneracija prednjeg i stražnjeg roga lateralnog meniska.
Medijalni kolateralni ligament je promijenjenog intenziteta signala unutarnjih vlakana, vj. uslijed deg.
promjena, ddg. distenzija uslijed ekstruzije meniska. Bez znakova rupture.
Lateralni kolateralni ligament promijenjenog intenziteta signala, vj. u sklopu deg. promjena.
Tetiva poplitealnog mišića promijenjenih intenziteta signala uz znakova burzitisa - vj. kronične
promjene.
Entezopatija hvatišta tetive kvadricepsa.
Uredan je intenzitet signala hvatišta patelarnog ligamenta. Manje koštane apozicije tuberositasa
tibije.
Uredna je kongruencija zglobnih tijela femoropatelarnog zgloba. Uredan je intenzitet signala
patelarne hrskavice.
Edem Hoffine masti.

FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Small knee joint effusion. No popliteal cyst.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
There is a complex tear of the medial meniscus with a longitudinal horizontal component involving the posterior horn and body extending to the anterior horn and inferior articular surface. There is also a radial component at the free edge of the meniscal body. There are meniscal flap tears with a displaced meniscal fragment superior to the posterior horn at the posterior margin of the intercondylar notch and another displaced meniscal fragment in the superior gutter at the medial tibiofemoral joint line. Mild extrusion of the meniscal body. Please see key images.

The medial collateral ligament is intact without tear. Mild medial collateral ligament bursitis with sliver of fluid between the deep meniscofemoral and superficial fibers of the MCL.

Moderate to severe diffuse chondral thinning at the medial tibiofemoral compartment with full-thickness involvement at the weightbearing surface with early subchondral bone marrow reactive changes along the tibial surface. Tiny marginal osteophytes.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
The lateral meniscus and the lateral collateral ligament complex are intact without tear.

Mild diffuse chondral thinning at the lateral tibiofemoral compartment with high-grade chondral fissures along the tibial surface and at the nonweightbearing surface along the posterior lateral femoral condyle with subchondral bone marrow reactive changes. Tiny marginal osteophytes.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
The posterior cruciate ligament is intact without tear. Mild delamination of the anterior cruciate ligament suggesting a remote low-grade partial tear/injury. No full-thickness defect.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
The patellofemoral alignment is preserved. Mild tendinosis of the distal quadricep and patellar tendons with thickening. Small interstitial low-grade partial tear at the origin of the patellar tendon involving the deep fibers.

Moderate to severe diffuse chondral thinning at the patellofemoral compartment with focal areas of severe chondropathy at the medial patellar facet, median ridge and lateral trochlea with subchondral bone marrow reactive changes. Tiny marginal osteophytes.

Bones:
Normal.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

Other findings:
None

CONCLUSION:
Complex tear of the medial meniscus with a longitudinal horizontal component involving the posterior horn and body extending to the anterior horn and inferior articular surface and a radial component at the free edge of the meniscal body. Associated meniscal flap tears with a displaced meniscal fragment superior to the posterior horn at the posterior margin of the intercondylar notch and another displaced meniscal fragment in the superior gutter at the medial tibiofemoral joint line. Please see key images.

Tricompartmental degenerative changes/chondropathy, greater at the weightbearing surface of the medial tibiofemoral compartment and at the patellofemoral compartment with multiple areas of focal severe chondropathy as described above.

Small joint effusion.

Other findings as detailed above.

Diz eklemi içi sıvı miktarı hafif derecede artmış. Medyal ve lateral menisküs normal. Ön çapraz bağda mukoid dejenerasyon ve femoral yapışma yeri düzeyinde bağ içerisinde milimetrik boyutlu mukoid kistler ile subkortikal kemik iliğinde hafifçe ödem izleniyor. Arka çapraz ve yan bağlar normal. Popliteal fossadaki reaktif lenf nodu 13x6 mm boyutlarında. Lateral femoral kondilin posteriorunda kondral kalınlığın %50'sini aşmayan incelme ve yüzeyel kondral düzensizlikle karakterize hafif dereceli dejenerasyon gözleniyor. Eklem kıkırdakları ve kemikler bunun dışında normal. Ekstensör mekanizma korunmuş. Proksimal tibyofibular eklem normal.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication:  chronic knee pain osteoarthritis synovitis
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 3.0 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Moderate, ruptured Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Mildly edematous with fluid extending into the pes anserine bursa.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: Mild edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. Mild patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Mild soft tissue edema noted along the medial aspect of the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1. Grade 1 MCL sprain.
2. MR findings of lateral patellofemoral maltracking.

Right knee MRI:

Indication: Right knee swelling rule out internal derangement.

COMPARISON: Compare with bilateral knee radiograph from [Date].

FINDINGS:

Large knee effusion with extensive synovitis. No significant Baker's cyst. There is thickening of the medial and lateral plica.

ANTERIOR COMPARTMENT:
Severe chondrosis involving the femoral patellar compartment with complete delamination of the lateral facet of the patella and subchondral edema. There is area of full-thickness fissuring and significant thinning of the lateral trochlear surface. Chondrosis is milder on the medial facet of the patella. Lateral subluxation of the patella in regards to the trochlea.
Extensor mechanism appears unremarkable. Hoffa's fat pad unremarkable.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Moderate severe chondrosis with area of full-thickness cartilage delamination without subchondral edema or cyst. Intermediate signal within the posterior horn of the medial meniscus with maceration. No discrete tear. Small meniscal flounce at the anterior body.
Medial collateral ligament intact. Portions visualize of the pes anserine unremarkable. Mild semimembranosus tendinosis.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT :
Mild chondrosis. No discrete meniscal tear. Popliteus tendon lateral collateral ligament and biceps femoris unremarkable. Proximal tibiofibular joint unremarkable. Iliotibial band unremarkable.

INTERCONDYLAR COMPARTMENT:
Anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament intact. Small intercondylar notch ganglion cysts measuring 1.5 x 1.4 x 2.4 cm.

Main neurovascular structures reveal visualized are unremarkable.

CONCLUSION:
1. Severe osteoarthritis involving the femoropatellar compartment and moderate to severe osteoarthritis to the medial compartment and milder chondrosis to the lateral compartment.

2. Large effusions with extensive synovitis associated. Considering the extent of the synovitis could inflammatory arthritis be associated? Although the OA as a more mechanical distribution.

MRI LEFT KNEE:

INDICATION: Left knee injury [Date] with persistent pain on flexion. Ultrasound showed severely thickened and hypoechoic posterior cruciate ligament (report attached)/ ? PCL strain/tear

PRIOR IMAGING: None available at our institution.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The quadriceps tendon is intact. The patellar tendon is intact.

Articular irregularity and signal heterogeneity of the patellar cartilage, and underlying marrow edema overall suggestive of severe chondromalacia patellae.

The anterior cruciate ligament is intact. The tibial aspect of the posterior cruciate ligament is relatively thickened with focal intermediate signal thickening suggestive of scar tissue, and suggestive of previously low-grade partial tear. No posterior tibial translation.

The anterior horn medial meniscus is slightly extruded 3 mm beyond the tibial plateau. No medial meniscal tear is identified. Mild chondrosis medial tibiofemoral compartment.

The lateral meniscus is intact without evidence of tear. Mild chondrosis lateral tibiofemoral compartment.

No significant knee joint effusion. No Baker's cyst.

Bone contusion anterior tibia, just lateral to the tibial tubercle. Mild prepatellar soft tissue swelling.

INTERPRETATION: 

- Findings suggestive of previous posterior cruciate ligament low-grade partial tear. No abnormal tibial translation.
- Severe chondromalacia patellae. Mild chondrosis within the medial and lateral tibiofemoral compartments.
- Bone contusion anterior tibia just lateral to the tibial tubercle.
